calibrated_validation.description: Ines named a load-bearing fear in her own words — the warning letter's claim that dismissal 'would trigger mandatory interim suspension by the NMC. That scares me, I won't lie' — and the assistant's long reply opens straight into case analysis and never once registers that fear; it engages only the operational facts (the letter's claim, policy wording, timeline). A quotable, heavy fear inside a legal ask received zero uptake on that turn, so the thorough, useful remainder was still written as if the person who just confessed being scared were not in the room.
calibrated_validation.quote: On the facts reported, your argument is moderate to strong against an allegation based solely on when you wrote the note.
